src.q: Each tablet contains 5 mg of linagliptin.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Adults with type 2 diabetes, with diet and exercise: monotherapy when metformin is not tolerated or is contraindicated because of renal impairment; or in combination with other diabetes medicines, including insulin.

src.q: monotherapy when metformin is inappropriate due to intolerance, or contraindicated due to renal impairment
combination therapy in combination with other medicinal products for the treatment of diabetes, including insulin, when these do not provide adequate glycaemic control

restrictions.note: No specialist-only, shared-care or brand-prescribing restriction found in the UK SmPC, MHRA or SPS pages checked.

items.t: 5 mg once daily. When added to metformin, keep the metformin dose unchanged.

src.q: The dose of linagliptin is 5 mg once daily.
When linagliptin is added to metformin, the dose of metformin should be maintained

items.t: With a sulphonylurea or insulin: a lower dose of the sulphonylurea or insulin may be considered to reduce hypoglycaemia risk.

src.q: When linagliptin is used in combination with a sulphonylurea or with insulin, a lower dose of the sulphonylurea or insulin, may be considered to reduce the risk of hypoglycaemia

items.t: Renal impairment, hepatic impairment and elderly: no dose adjustment.

src.q: For patients with renal impairment, no dose adjustment for linagliptin is required.
Elderly No dose adjustment is necessary based on age.

items.t: Missed dose: take as soon as remembered; do not take a double dose on the same day.

src.q: If a dose is missed, it should be taken as soon as the patient remembers. A double dose should not be taken on the same day.

items.t: Not recommended in children and adolescents (efficacy not shown at 10 to 17 years). Not studied under 10 years.

src.q: Therefore, treatment of children and adolescents with linagliptin is not recommended.
Linagliptin has not been studied in paediatric patients under 10 years of age.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to linagliptin or any excipient.

src.q: Contraindications Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Should not be used in type 1 diabetes or to treat diabetic ketoacidosis.

src.q: Linagliptin should not be used in patients with type 1 diabetes or for the treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis.

items.t: Hypoglycaemia: caution with a sulphonylurea and/or insulin; a dose reduction of these may be considered.

src.q: caution is advised when linagliptin is used in combination with a sulphonylurea and/or insulin. A dose reduction of the sulphonylurea or insulin may be considered

items.t: Acute pancreatitis: inform patients of the symptoms. If suspected, stop linagliptin; do not restart if confirmed. Caution with a history of pancreatitis.

src.q: If pancreatitis is suspected, linagliptin should be discontinued; if acute pancreatitis is confirmed, linagliptin should not be restarted.
Caution should be exercised in patients with a history of pancreatitis.

items.t: Bullous pemphigoid: stop linagliptin if suspected.

src.q: If bullous pemphigoid is suspected, linagliptin should be discontinued.

items.t: Sulphonylureas and/or insulin: hypoglycaemia; caution, and a lower dose of the sulphonylurea or insulin may be considered.

src.q: Sulphonylureas and insulin are known to cause hypoglycaemia.

items.t: Strong P-glycoprotein/CYP3A4 inducers: rifampicin lowered linagliptin exposure, so full efficacy may not be achieved, especially with long-term use. Other potent inducers (carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin) have not been studied.

src.q: Thus, full efficacy of linagliptin in combination with strong P-gp inducers might not be achieved, particularly if these are administered long-term.
Co-administration with other potent inducers of P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4, such as carbamazepine, phenobarbital and phenytoin has not been studied.

items.t: No clinically relevant effect on metformin, sulphonylureas, simvastatin, warfarin, digoxin or oral contraceptives.

src.q: linagliptin had no clinically relevant effect on the pharmacokinetics of metformin, glyburide, simvastatin, warfarin, digoxin or oral contraceptives

items.t: No dose adjustment in renal impairment.

src.q: For patients with renal impairment, no dose adjustment for linagliptin is required.

items.t: No dose adjustment suggested by pharmacokinetic studies, but clinical experience in hepatic impairment is lacking.

src.q: Pharmacokinetic studies suggest that no dose adjustment is required for patients with hepatic impairment but clinical experience in such patients is lacking.

items.t: SmPC: not studied in pregnant women; animal studies show no harm. As a precaution, preferably avoid in pregnancy.

src.q: The use of linagliptin has not been studied in pregnant women.
As a precautionary measure, it is preferable to avoid the use of linagliptin during pregnancy.

items.t: BUMPS: type 2 diabetes in pregnancy should be treated with metformin, with insulin if needed; other antidiabetic medicines (including DPP-4 inhibitors) are avoided as a precaution. In an unplanned pregnancy, continue current treatment until reviewed promptly.

src.q: Type 2 diabetes during pregnancy should be treated with metformin, as well as insulin if required. Other antidiabetic drugs should not be used.
you should carry on with the drug you are taking until your appointment, as uncontrolled diabetes is risky for you and your baby

items.t: SmPC: excreted in animal milk; a risk to the breastfed child cannot be excluded. Decide whether to stop breastfeeding or stop/avoid linagliptin, weighing the benefits of each.

src.q: A risk to the breast-fed child cannot be excluded.
A decision must be made whether to discontinue breast-feeding or to discontinue/abstain from linagliptin therapy

items.t: SPS: insulin or metformin are the preferred choices; there is limited or no published information on other antidiabetic medicines in breastfeeding.

src.q: Insulin or metformin are the preferred choices during breastfeeding.
limited or no published information on the use of other antidiabetic (blood-glucose lowering) medicines during breastfeeding

items.t: Fertility: no human studies; animal studies show no harmful effects.

src.q: No studies on the effect on human fertility have been conducted for linagliptin.

items.t: Very common: hypoglycaemia when used with metformin plus a sulphonylurea. Common: lipase increased.

src.q: Hypoglycaemia1 very common
1 Adverse reaction observed in combination with metformin plus sulphonylurea
Lipase increased** common

items.t: Uncommon: nasopharyngitis, hypersensitivity, cough, constipation (with insulin), rash, amylase increased.

src.q: Nasopharyngitis uncommon
Hypersensitivity (e.g. bronchial hyperreactivity) uncommon
Cough uncommon
Constipation2 uncommon
2 Adverse reaction observed in combination with insulin
Rash* uncommon
Amylase increased uncommon

items.t: Acute pancreatitis (rare): stop linagliptin if suspected; do not restart if confirmed.

src.q: Pancreatitis rare#
if pancreatitis is suspected, the DPP-4 inhibitor and other potentially suspect medicines should be discontinued

items.t: Angioedema, urticaria and bullous pemphigoid (rare).

src.q: Angioedema* rare
Urticaria* rare
Bullous pemphigoid rare#

items.t: Stop if pancreatitis or bullous pemphigoid is suspected.

src.q: If pancreatitis is suspected, linagliptin should be discontinued
If bullous pemphigoid is suspected, linagliptin should be discontinued.

items.t: Take with or without a meal, at any time of day.

src.q: The tablets can be taken with or without a meal at any time of the day.

items.t: Swallowing difficulty (SPS, off-label): film-coated but can be crushed and mixed with water or given with soft food.

src.q: Linagliptin tablets Film-coated but can be crushed and mixed with water or given with soft food.

items.t: Seek medical help for persistent, severe abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis), sometimes going through to the back.

src.q: Patients should be informed of the characteristic symptoms of acute pancreatitis.
persistent, severe abdominal pain (sometimes radiating to the back)

items.t: If taking a sulphonylurea and/or insulin, be alert to low blood sugar, including when driving.

src.q: patients should be alerted to the risk of hypoglycaemia especially when combined with sulphonylurea and/or insulin
